findings.title: A render that straddles the running-window boundary leaves 'Running now' at 'session active' after the header shows Idle, until the next store change (AC-60 edge case)

evidence.value: const clockState = now => `${forecastIsPast(now)} ${isLive()} ${scopeLive()}`;  (only the forecast part uses the render's reading; isLive()/scopeLive() reach sessionLive, which reads Date.now() again)
const sessionLive = s => !!s && (s.running > 0 || Date.now() - new Date(s.last) < (Number(s.windowMinutes) || 10) * 60000);
the tile reads sessionLive(s) while the Overview is drawn; drawnClock = clockState(now) reads the clock again after every tab is drawn

A store snapshot re-renders 1 ms before the 10-minute window elapses, and the boundary passes after the Overview is drawn. After 3 minute ticks: header=Idle, tile=["0","session active"]. drawnClock already recorded idle, so the timer never redraws.

findings.impact: AC-60 requires 'session idle' within 60 s of the header showing Idle. If the window elapses between the Overview draw and the drawnClock reading, drawnClock records idle while the tile shows active. Every later tick then finds no difference, and the tile stays wrong until a store change, which may not come for an idle session. That needs a render in progress at the boundary, a window of a few milliseconds, so it is rare. The same mismatch applies to the Dispatch tile's live/paused, which comes from scopeLive().
findings.remediation: Use one clock reading per render for the live state as well as the forecast. For example, give sessionLive an optional now (defaulting to Date.now()), have isLive and scopeLive pass it through, and have the renderers and clockState use renderNow during renderAll while the timer's comparison passes its own reading. Add a page check that straddles the window the way the forecast one-reading check straddles the forecast time.

findings.title: usage.hourly entries with an hour but no numeric main/sub still draw an SVG full of NaN, a garbled chart instead of 'No hourly data'

evidence.value: const hours = (Array.isArray(u.hourly) ? u.hourly : []).filter(h => h && typeof h.hour === 'string');
hourly [{hour:'2026-09-10T10'},{hour:'2026-09-10T11',main:'x',sub:null}]: NaN in the usage chart markup, no error state, 0 console.error

findings.impact: This does not crash, which is what the follow-up asked for, and the exporter (trusted, internal input) writes numbers. But the entry check covers the member only by its hour key. A leaf of the wrong type makes max NaN, so every gridline and bar coordinate is NaN. The browser rejects the attributes and logs SVG errors, and the chart comes out garbled.
findings.remediation: Normalise the leaves as well, for example map each kept entry to { hour, main: Number(h.main) || 0, sub: Number(h.sub) || 0 }. Add a missing or non-numeric main/sub case to the existing usage.hourly page check.
